text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois are frequently targeted by digital and phone scams, most notably fake text messages about unpaid traffic or tollway fines, phishing alerts about held mail packages, and imposter scams involving government or tech support.

list.snippet: Fake Toll and Traffic Texts: Scammers send texts claiming you owe money for a missed toll or traffic violation, threatening a license suspension if you do not click a link to pay.
Delivery/Package Smishing: Text messages pretend to be from the USPS or UPS, claiming a package cannot be delivered unless you click a link to update your address or pay a small fee.
Government and Agency Imposters: Con artists call or text pretending to be from the IRS, Social Security Administration, or local law enforcement, demanding immediate payment or personal data.
Online Purchase and Pet Scams: Fraudulent online storefronts or fake pet adoption listings take money via unverified methods for items or companion animals that never arrive.
Tech Support Pop-ups: Fake browser warnings or calls claim your computer or phone has a virus and demand remote access or payment to fix it.
Do not click links: Never tap or click links found in unsolicited text messages or unexpected emails.

Verify independently: Government agencies do not text or call asking for unprompted payments or sensitive personal details. Look up official contact numbers independently rather than using the number provided in a suspicious message.
Practice the pause: Take a moment to step back when faced with an urgent request demanding secrecy or immediate payment.

Check resources: Report or look up active local trends using the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or file a complaint with the Office of the Illinois Attorney General
.
